taskDescription: Click every word in the passage that names a protein encoded by the HIV genome.
textField: HIV attaches to host cells using *gp120*, which binds the CD4 receptor, and *gp41*, which drives membrane fusion. The *p24* capsid encloses two copies of the RNA genome and three viral enzymes. Reverse transcriptase copies RNA into DNA, *integrase* inserts the proviral DNA into the host chromosome, and *protease* cleaves the Gag-Pol polyprotein so that new virions can mature.

overallFeedback.feedback: gp120 (CD4 binding), gp41 (membrane fusion), p24 (capsid protein used in rapid diagnostic assays), integrase (proviral insertion, target of dolutegravir) and protease (polyprotein cleavage, target of ritonavir) are all HIV-encoded proteins. CD4 is a host receptor, not a viral protein. Reverse transcriptase is also a viral enzyme but appears here as a two-word compound name.
